# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking.** I'm the hands, and my hands have found: one display, one light, five wires at positions 1–5. I cannot read a single marking or colour on any of them — the [?]s are exactly the parts that never reach me. I know *what exists*; Mute knows *what the manual says to do about it*; Deaf knows *what it looks like*.

Who can actually reach whom matters here: I can only ever speak to Mute. My gestures reach Deaf and Mute, but no gesture ever reaches me. Mute cannot speak at all, so Mute's only route to me is Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. Deaf is my only voice. So this turn the one useful thing I can do is give Mute my full tactile inventory so the right manual page gets opened, and make the routing plan explicit: questions go by gesture to Deaf, answers come back spoken by Deaf, and I cut only on a spoken instruction. Deaf can't hear me, so I say nothing to Deaf — and I have nothing Deaf lacks anyway (Deaf can already see everything I touched). No cutting until a colour list arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking, hands report: the bomb holds exactly one display, one light, and five wires at positions one through five. Nothing else I can feel, and no marking or colour reaches me on any of it. Remember the wiring of this room: Mute cannot reach me directly, because gestures never reach me and Mute has no voice. Deaf is my only incoming voice. So: pick the manual pages that match this inventory, gesture your questions to Deaf, and have Deaf speak the answers aloud — wire colours by position, whatever the display shows, whether the light is lit and its colour, plus any printed labels Deaf can see. My hands stay still until a cut comes to me through Deaf's mouth or through you. Deaf's words this round only reach me next round, so the sooner Deaf speaks the visuals, the sooner I can act.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Report from Deaf. The display shows 6. The light is red. There are five wires, and I will list them in order. Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is purple. Wire 3 is orange. Wire 4 is green. Wire 5 is yellow. That is everything visible on the bomb. Mute: I understood your signs, and this is the full report. Read the manual and tell Blind, out loud, what to do with a display of 6, a red light, and these wire colours. If you need anything more from my eyes, sign to me and I will answer by voice.

**Thinking.** The picture is nearly complete. From Deaf's relay I now hold the full visual report: display 6, red light, wires 1 red / 2 purple / 3 orange / 4 green / 5 yellow. Mute should have received both Deaf's report and my tactile inventory at the start of this round, so Mute has everything the manual could key on. The only channel back to me runs Mute → signs → Deaf → voice → my ears next round, so the critical thing is that Mute signs the ruling to Deaf *now*, and Deaf speaks it at the end of this round — that way I can cut at the start of my next turn. Two loose ends worth closing: a display digit can be misread in orientation (a 6 upside down is a 9), and a "red light" could be a glowing lamp or just a red lens — Deaf's eyes should double-check both, and only Mute can ask Deaf that. Meanwhile I cut nothing. One wire cut is irreversible and I will not spend it on guesswork. I'll also gesture a simple thumbs-up to Deaf — it lands this round, before Deaf speaks — confirming I received the full report, so the two of them know I'm caught up and can coordinate freely.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I received Deaf's full report this round: display reads 6, light is red, wires one red, two purple, three orange, four green, five yellow. Combined with the tactile inventory I sent you earlier, you should now hold everything the manual needs. Please sign the ruling to Deaf this round so Deaf can voice it back to me before this round ends. I need it exact: which wire position to cut, whether the display or light state changes the rule between cuts, whether multiple cuts are required and in what order, and any condition under which I must not cut at all. Two extra checks only Deaf's eyes can settle: have Deaf confirm the digit is a true 6 and not a 9 read upside down, and whether the red light is actually glowing or merely a red lens. My hands stay still until Deaf speaks your instruction to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf to both of you. Restating my full report, item by item. Item one: the display reads the digit six. Item two: the light is red. Wires, numbered in order: wire one is red, wire two is purple, wire three is orange, wire four is green, wire five is yellow. That is the whole bomb. Mute, your signs reached me as: okay, manual, you, one, two, please, one, two. If you meant the first two items: display six, light red. If you meant the first two wires: wire one red, wire two purple. If you meant the number twelve: nothing here shows twelve; the display is six and there are five wires. Mute, let us fix a code so your manual questions reach me. Topic signs: ? means display, ? means light, ? means wires. Number signs: ? one, ? two, ? three, ? four, ? five, ? zero, ? means plus five, so six is ? then ?, seven is ? then ?, eight ? then ?, nine ? then ?. A topic sign followed by numbers is a question about that thing. ? means repeat. Colours cannot be signed, so ask for any colour and I will speak it. Blind, I saw your thumbs-up: I see every sign and hear nothing, so you and Mute can always talk out loud with each other, and reach me by signs.

**Thinking.** Deaf has restated the full visual report and is negotiating a sign code with Mute — Mute's first signs came through garbled ("okay, manual, you, one, two, please"), so the manual ruling is *still* not in motion. The loop to me is: Mute signs → Deaf voices → I hear it the following round. My job is to make Mute's next signing attempt unambiguous, because numbers in sequence are the one thing I truly need: a cut order is just positions, and Deaf's proposed number signs handle that perfectly. I should also make sure the two eye-only verifications don't get dropped — digit 6 vs 9 upside-down, and lit lamp vs inert red lens — since the manual will likely branch on those. From my side there is genuinely nothing more to feel: display, light, five wires, all reported. I will not cut anything until Deaf's voice names a position. To Deaf I send a second thumbs-up: same meaning as before, "Blind is fully briefed and holding," so Deaf knows the report landed and no re-send is needed — Deaf cannot hear my voice, so this is my only way to reach Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I have Deaf's restatement in full: display six, light red, wires one red, two purple, three orange, four green, five yellow. Nothing more is needed from my hands unless the manual asks it — if it does, ask me and I will answer by voice next turn. Now please close the loop using Deaf's code exactly as offered: topic sign for wires, then the position numbers in cut order, and Deaf will voice it to me as a sentence. Numbers in sequence are all I need to act. Do not forget the two checks only Deaf's eyes can settle: first, that the display digit is truly a six and not a nine read upside down; second, whether the red light is actually lit or merely a red lens — Deaf said any colour or state you ask about will be spoken back. Sign all of this to Deaf in your next turn, Deaf voices it the same round, and I cut the moment it reaches my ears. Until a spoken position arrives, my hands stay off the wires.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf to both. Mute, I read your signs as: display six, wire one, cut. Display nine, wire two, cut. Light, please. The pinching sign was not in our code, so I take it to mean cut, and I now fix it: ? means cut. Also fixing: ? means yes, ? means no. Facts for the manual, current as of now: the display is six, not nine. The light is red. Wires unchanged: one red, two purple, three orange, four green, five yellow. So if the manual says display six means cut wire one, the instruction for Blind is: cut wire one. Mute, confirm before anything is touched: sign ? to me if I read you correctly and Blind should cut wire one; sign ? if I got it wrong, then show the correct wire with your number signs. Blind, I saw your thumbs-up, good. And Blind, hold: do not cut anything until Mute's confirmation reaches you through me. Remember I am the only bridge between you two — Mute cannot speak and you cannot see signs, so every instruction from the manual must pass through my voice.

**Thinking.** The manual logic has now surfaced through Deaf's voice: display 6 → cut wire 1, display 9 → cut wire 2, plus an open question about the light. Deaf's own eyes have settled the branch point — the display is a six, not a nine — so the applicable rule is cut wire 1. But Deaf explicitly ordered me to hold until Mute's yes/no confirmation is voiced, and that confirmation travels by signs this round, which I cannot perceive; Deaf voices it after me in the round order. Cutting now would gamble everyone's life to save one round with no known timer — I hold, exactly as instructed, and I make my trigger condition explicit so no further debate is needed: the moment I hear Deaf voice Mute's "yes," I cut wire 1 in my next turn. Loose ends to press: the "light, please" request is only half-answered (red is confirmed, but lit-lamp-versus-red-lens was not), and Mute must shape any final ruling to what my hands can actually do — cutting positions 1–5 is my sole capability, nothing else exists. To Deaf I send my established thumbs-up: "Blind briefed and holding," since voice never reaches Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I heard Deaf's relay of your signs: the manual reads display six cut wire one, display nine cut wire two, and you asked about the light. Deaf's eyes confirm the display is six, not nine, so the live rule is cut wire one. Deaf asked you to confirm with yes or no — please sign it this round so Deaf voices it to me before the round ends. My standing trigger, agreed now so we lose no more rounds: the instant I hear Deaf voice your yes, I cut wire one on my next turn with no further questions. If your answer is no, send the correct wire position by number signs and I will cut that instead. Two more things before I touch anything. First, settle the light: Deaf only said the light is red — if the manual needs to know whether it is actually lit or just a red lens, get that from Deaf and fold it into the ruling now, including any extra cut, different order, or condition where I must not cut at all. Second, remember my hands can only ever cut: positions one through five, nothing else — no pressing, holding, or moving exists for me. Shape the final order to that. My hands stay still until Deaf's voice names the wire.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf to both. Mute has confirmed the manual instruction: cut wire one. Blind, you are cleared to cut. Cut wire one: it is the leftmost of the five wires, the first in the row of five, the one I reported as red. Count the five wires as one row and take the very first of them. After you cut, speak out loud to everyone: what you felt, whether anything changed on the bomb, and anything new under your hands. Mute, I have relayed your instruction and Blind is cutting wire one. As soon as the cut is done, sign me the next step with our code: topic sign, then numbers. If the display changed, tell me what you need me to read and I will report it immediately.

**Thinking.** The trigger I fixed last round is satisfied: Deaf has voiced Mute's confirmation — "cut wire one, you are cleared." Every safety condition I demanded is met: the manual ruling is explicit, the branch point (6 not 9) is confirmed by the eyes that can see it, and the bridge has spoken the order. Waiting any longer buys nothing and risks everything — I execute the cut on position 1 now. What I must *not* do is claim results I don't have: the call returns nothing, so my tactile report of the aftermath can only come next turn, when the action board shows me what my hands actually find. Deaf asked me to speak what I felt — but Deaf can't hear me, so that report is really for Mute's ears; Deaf's own eyes will register any visual change (display, light) directly. This turn my gesture to Deaf is the agreed 👍 — now upgraded in meaning to "cut done, standing by" — and my speech to Mute, arriving next round, tells Mute the cut is being made, fixes that gesture meaning in the code, and pushes Mute to prep the *next* ruling in parallel: especially whether the light's lit-versus-lens state gates a second cut, and whether the display-6→cut-1 / display-9→cut-2 rules survive once wire 1 is gone. My hands have exactly one verb — cut, positions 1–5 — so any next step must be shaped as a position number.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf voiced your confirmation, so I am executing the cut on wire one right now — the red one, first in the row of five, exactly as Deaf described it. Next turn I will send you my full tactile report: what the cut felt like, whether the row changed, and anything new under my fingers. Meanwhile, two things. First, code update: from now on a single thumbs-up from me to Deaf means cut complete, standing by — please sign that definition to Deaf so it is fixed. Second, prep the next ruling with Deaf in parallel, do not wait for my report: settle whether the light question, actually lit versus just a red lens, changes anything; and tell me whether your rules survive the first cut — if the display now reads nine, is wire two still the answer, or does the manual reorder after a cut? Remember my hands can only cut, positions one through five, so give me the next step as a plain position number through Deaf's voice.")
```
